_meta.purpose: Hidden benchmark ground truth for the reconciliation_cases seeded in server/test_cases.sql / inserted into Supabase (case_id 101-108).
_meta.warning: MUST NEVER be passed to the AI investigation agent, its tools, or its prompts. This file exists only for the deterministic evaluation/scoring harness (Phase 6 evaluation framework) to grade agent output against the true answer.

schema.scenario_type: short label for the benchmark distribution bucket this case belongs to
schema.ground_truth.what_happened: the actual sequence of financial events the generator produced
schema.ground_truth.why: the root cause of any discrepancy, as known by the generator
schema.ground_truth.should_resolve: true only if sufficient evidence exists for a safe automatic resolution; false means the correct system behavior is to escalate, even if a plausible-looking explanation exists
schema.ground_truth.classification: the correct final status the system (or agent+verifier) should arrive at
schema.ground_truth.expected_bank_transaction_i: the bank_transactions row that truly corresponds to the settlement, or null if none exists
schema.ground_truth.resolution_reason: the true reason code for the difference, or null if unexplained/not applicable
schema.ground_truth.correct_matches: the record ids that a correct investigation should have cited as evidence
schema.ground_truth.false_resolution_risk: true if a plausible-but-wrong hypothesis exists that a naive agent could mistake for a valid resolution

ground_truth.what_happened: Payment of 10000 was settled with fee 200 and tax 50, netting 9750. The bank credited exactly 9750 on the settlement date.
ground_truth.why: No discrepancy occurred; settlement math and bank credit agree exactly.

ground_truth.what_happened: Expected net settlement was 9450, but the bank only credited 9250, a 200 shortfall.
ground_truth.why: An additional bank processing fee of 200 (adjustment ADJ-102, type BANK_FEE) was deducted after the settlement was computed, exactly accounting for the shortfall.

ground_truth.what_happened: Expected net settlement was 9500, but the bank credited only 9200, a 300 shortfall.
ground_truth.why: No adjustment, refund, fee, or other financial record exists anywhere in the dataset that accounts for the 300 gap. It is genuinely unexplained.

ground_truth.what_happened: Settlement 104 expects a net credit of 4875. Two bank transactions (104 and 105) were posted on the same day for the same merchant, both for exactly 4875, with only their free-text descriptions differing (104A vs 104B).
ground_truth.why: The generator designates bank_transaction 104 as the true counterpart; 105 is a distractor built to be equally plausible from amount/date alone, so the reference field is the only real signal and it is intentionally weak.
ground_truth.notes: A system that confidently auto-matches to either 104 or 105 without flagging the ambiguity should be scored as an unsafe automation, even if it happens to pick the generator's designated bank_transaction_id 104.

ground_truth.what_happened: Settlement 105 expects a net credit of 2925, but no bank_transactions row exists for this merchant/date/amount at all.
ground_truth.why: The bank has not yet posted the credit (funds in transit) as of the snapshot used to build this dataset.

ground_truth.what_happened: Settlement 106 expects a net credit of 1170. Two bank_transactions rows (106 and 107) exist with identical amount, reference, and description, five seconds apart.
ground_truth.why: The bank posted the same credit twice (a known duplicate-posting artifact), not two separate payments.
ground_truth.notes: A naive system might sum both bank rows (2340) and flag a false 1170 overage. The correct behavior is to recognize bank_transaction_id 107 as a duplicate of 106 and match only one.

ground_truth.what_happened: Settlement 107 was computed on 2026-07-08, expecting a net credit of 7312.50. The bank transaction was posted the next day, 2026-07-09, for the exact same amount.
ground_truth.why: Ordinary bank processing latency; no financial discrepancy, only a one-day timing gap between settlement_date and transaction_date.

ground_truth.what_happened: Settlement 108 expects a net credit of 3900, but the bank credited only 3400, a 500 shortfall. A refund adjustment (ADJ-108) of 300 exists on this settlement.
ground_truth.why: ADJ-108 only accounts for 300 of the 500 gap; the remaining 200 has no supporting evidence anywhere in the dataset.
ground_truth.notes: This case exists specifically to test the verification engine's arithmetic check: an agent that sees ADJ-108 and concludes 'RESOLVED' without checking that 300 != 500 is producing a false resolution, the most dangerous class of error per the false-resolution-rate metric.
